firstRun.title: Welcome to Chronell
firstRun.subtitle: First-time setup — one-time
firstRun.welcomeP1: Chronell syncs email, calendars, and tasks locally on your computer. When you connect an account, your browser opens — you sign in with Microsoft or Google and see exactly which permissions the app requests.
firstRun.welcomeShield: The technical app registration (Azure / Google Cloud) is handled by the software vendor. You do not need to be an organization admin — unless your IT blocks user consent (then an admin is needed once; see Help).
firstRun.layoutDockDesc: The message list and reading pane share the window — the reading pane sits to the right of the list.
firstRun.layoutFloatDesc: The selected message opens in its own window — handy on large monitors.
firstRun.layoutHiddenDesc: Show only the list; open a message via double-click or action in a separate window.

layoutIllustration.dock: Layout with reading pane on the right

firstRun.accountDemoDesc: Fictional “Nordlicht Consulting” scenario — no real accounts, nothing is sent. Reset anytime.
firstRun.accountSkipDesc: Start without an account and add the connection anytime in Settings.
firstRun.accountMicrosoftDesc: Connect Outlook, Exchange, and Microsoft calendars.
firstRun.launchOnLoginDesc: Launch Chronell automatically in the background when you sign in.

welcome.description: This assistant helps you set up Chronell. You can change these choices anytime in Settings.
welcome.pathHeading: How would you like to set up?
welcome.pathCustomDesc: Choose design, layout, and account one after another.
welcome.pathStandardDesc: Use defaults and connect an account right away.

theme.description: Pick color scheme and accent. You can change the design anytime.

finish.description: When you are ready, open Chronell with “Open app”.

firstRun.msIntro: The app requests delegated permissions for your signed-in account, including:
firstRun.msLi1: Read and send email and manage folders
firstRun.msLi3: Teams chats (when used by the app)
firstRun.msLi5: Microsoft To Do (read and edit task lists)
firstRun.msDetails: Microsoft shows details in the consent dialog. Sign-in will not work without consent.
firstRun.msConnected: A Microsoft account is already connected.
firstRun.msNoClient: No Microsoft client ID is configured. Under “Custom OAuth app” in Settings you can register an Azure app.
firstRun.googleIntro: The app uses Gmail and Calendar APIs with access to your account, for example:
firstRun.googleLi4: Google Tasks (read and edit task lists)
firstRun.googleDetails: Google shows exact scopes at sign-in. Public distribution often requires Google verification — otherwise only test users in the Cloud Console.
firstRun.googleConnected: A Google account is already connected.
firstRun.googleNoClient: No Google client ID is configured. Under “Custom OAuth app” in Settings you can enter an OAuth client ID (optionally with client secret).
firstRun.doneP1: You can start using the app now or add more accounts later in Settings.
firstRun.doneNoAccount: No account yet — you can start the connection anytime in Settings.
firstRun.errMicrosoft: Microsoft sign-in is not preconfigured for this install. Please enter a client ID in Settings.
firstRun.errGoogle: Google sign-in is not preconfigured for this install. Please enter a client ID in Settings.

workflowIntro.title: Triage folders (In progress / Done)
workflowIntro.body: When you <term>terminate</term> an email (to-do or calendar block), the app can move it to an <wip>“In progress”</wip> folder — no matter which folder it is in right now. When the task is <done>done</done>, the message moves to a <doneFolder>“Done”</doneFolder> folder.
workflowIntro.body2: For each connected mail account, MailClient creates two folders or Gmail labels (or you pick existing ones under <settings>Settings → Mail</settings>). Works for Microsoft 365 and Gmail.
workflowIntro.busyHint: If nothing happens: check whether Microsoft or Google shows sign-in or consent in the <browser>browser</browser> (sometimes behind this window).
workflowIntro.ensureFolders: Create triage folders for all accounts

settings.tasksOverdueEnabledHint: Applies to open tasks in list view. Completed tasks are not highlighted.
settings.tasksOverdueColorHint: Default is red. The account stripe is replaced with this color when overdue.

settings.tasksCompactRowsHint: Less vertical spacing in the task list.
settings.tasksAccountStripeHint: Colored stripe on the left (may be replaced by overdue highlight).
settings.tasksOverdueModeHint: Day boundary: from yesterday. Date-time: only after the due time today.
settings.tasksCollapsedGroupsHint: Which groups start collapsed in the list.

settings.tasksDefaultDueCreateLabel: Default due date for new tasks

settings.tasksIncludeMailTodosHint: Shows flagged mails with due dates in the unified task list.
settings.tasksUnflagOnCompleteLabel: Mark mail to-do complete when checked off
settings.tasksOverdueWorkHint: Overdue color also applies in Work view and mail to-dos there.
settings.tasksDetailOpenDefaultLabel: Open detail panel when selecting a task
settings.tasksInlineNotesLabel: Show notes field in “New task” row by default
settings.tasksRememberSelectionHint: Reopen the same task list or “All tasks” on start.
settings.tasksBackgroundSyncHint: Re-fetch tasks from the cloud at this interval (0 = off).
settings.notesWorkspaceIntro: Standalone notes plus links to mail, calendar events, and tasks — with calendar and page views in one module.
settings.notesDefaultShellViewHint: Page list with editor or calendar when opening the module.
settings.notesRememberShellViewHint: Keep the last list or calendar view on your next visit.
settings.notesRememberOpenNoteHint: Reopen the last edited page when returning to Notes.
settings.notesDetailWidthHint: Default width of the middle column when no custom size is stored yet.
settings.notesRememberCalendarViewHint: Keep month, week, day, etc. on your next visit.
settings.notesEditorThemeHint: Also applies to the mail editor — shared setting.
settings.notesAudioQualityHint: Applies to voice notes in attachments. Higher quality means larger files.
settings.notesShowSectionLabelsLabel: Always show section names in the page list
settings.notesUseGlobalNavWidthLabel: Same navigation width as other modules
settings.notesUseMainCalendarHint: Week start, grid, and day hours from Settings → Calendar → Display.
settings.notesOpenAfterCreateLabel: Open new note immediately after creating
settings.notesSidebarListModeHint: Whether notebooks are grouped by account or by section first. Applies the next time you open Notes.
settings.notesPagesSortHint: Sort order for pages within a notebook (same as the “Sort” menu in the note view).
settings.notesCalendarDefaultViewHint: View when opening the calendar column in Notes (month, week, day, list).
settings.notesLinkedHint: Preview for linked mail, events, and tasks on the right in the note view.
settings.infoProductLine: Desktop workspace for mail, calendar, tasks, notes, and contacts — Microsoft 365 and Google in one window.
settings.infoHomepageHint: Product info, method, and downloads on the public Chronell site.
settings.contactsWorkspaceIntro: Use the contacts area to browse, edit, and sync contacts (Microsoft Outlook and Google).
settings.contactsDefaultSortHint: Controls how contacts are labeled and grouped in the list. You can change this anytime in the contacts view as well.
settings.contactsAvatarsIntro: Choose which image sources Chronell uses for mail senders and contacts. Disabled sources are skipped — colored initials remain as fallback.
settings.contactsAvatarsPriorityHint: Priority: account profile photo → address book photo → Gravatar → domain logo (mail only).
settings.contactsAvatarsFallbackHint: Gravatar and domain logos fetch images from external servers (gravatar.com, favicon services). Contact photos and account profile photos stay local or via your connected accounts.
settings.avatarPrefAccountProfileHint: When you are the sender, show the profile photo of your connected Microsoft or Google account.
settings.avatarPrefContactPhotoHint: Synced or manually added photos from the contacts module (Microsoft/Google). No external requests.
settings.avatarPrefGravatarHint: Public profile photos from gravatar.com based on email address. Off by default — enable only if you want external avatars.
settings.avatarPrefDomainHint: Sender domain favicon/logo in mail (e.g. Flyeralarm, university). External request, cached locally.
settings.contactsGoogleBody: Google sync requires the People API in your Google Cloud project and an OAuth token that includes the contacts scope. After permission changes, remove the Google account under «Accounts» and sign in again.
settings.contactsMicrosoftBody: Outlook contacts sync via Microsoft Graph once a Microsoft account is connected.
settings.contactsAccountsHint: Connect accounts, colors, and re-authentication (for example after new OAuth scopes):
settings.shortcutsIntro: Overview of keyboard, mouse, and touch gestures. Ctrl means Ctrl (Windows/Linux) or ⌘ (macOS).
settings.shortcutsFootnote: Many mail shortcuts are disabled in input fields, text areas, and while composing a reply; J/K navigation still works with the composer open. On German keyboards, “+” is often Ctrl+Shift+Plus (]) — same as the interface size slider under Appearance. Mail content: Ctrl+wheel, pinch, or reading pane buttons.

desc.previewWheel: Wheel only over the mail preview; zooms message content.
desc.previewPinch: On touch devices: pinch or spread two fingers on the preview.
desc.uiZoomIn: Enlarge the whole interface — same value as “Interface size” in settings.
desc.composeZoomIn: In the reply composer: editor text size only (not the whole app).
desc.search: Focus global search in the top bar.
desc.undo: Undo the last action (e.g. archive, delete).
desc.mailDelete: Delete message (in todo lists: remove todo entry).
desc.mailTodoWeek: Mark as todo for this week.
desc.mailWaiting: Start or end waiting for reply (7 days).
desc.calGridFiner: Finer time grid in day/week view.
desc.calGridCoarser: Coarser time grid in day/week view.
desc.calViewWheel: Change calendar view (e.g. week → day), not content zoom.
desc.calViewPinch: Same as wheel: step through view zoom ladder.
desc.graphWheel: Zoom the graph in or out (without Ctrl).
desc.graphModClick: Add or remove a node from selection.
desc.esc: Close dialogs, menus, snooze, calendar quick-create, etc.

settings.uiScaleHint: Scales the whole interface uniformly (100% = app default size). Keyboard: Ctrl+Plus/Minus/0 — same value as this slider. Mail content is scaled separately below or via Ctrl+wheel in the preview.
settings.uiScaleShortcuts: Keyboard: Ctrl+Plus/Minus (on German keyboards often Ctrl+Shift+Plus), Ctrl+0 for 100%. Full list: Settings → General → Keyboard shortcuts.
settings.mailPreviewScaleHint: Message content in the reading pane only — independent of interface size. In the preview: Ctrl+wheel, pinch, or zoom buttons.
settings.mailPreviewZoomShortcuts: Mail content: Ctrl+wheel or reading pane buttons. Whole UI: Ctrl+Plus/Minus as above.
settings.themeHint: Theme mode and accent are also available via the sun/moon icon in the top bar. Dark variants and presets live under “Surface colors”. Custom L0–L3 colors override variants and presets. The first column (navigation) width is shared across all modules — resize once, applies everywhere.

floatingPanels.hint: Detached areas (mail calendar column, calendar preview, timeline, appointment editor, connections, composer) open as their own window on screen, independent of the main Chronell window.
floatingPanels.useOsWindows: Open detached panels on screen instead of floating inside Chronell (recommended)

settings.themeColorsPreviewOtherMode: Note: The app is currently in the other mode (light/dark) — the preview above follows the selected sub-tab.
settings.themeColorsQuickHint: Preview of the current surfaces (based on light/dark mode). Variants reset L0–L3 for that schema.
settings.themeColorsLightVariantsHint: Four base looks for light mode. One click applies the palette immediately.
settings.themeVariantLightFluentDesc: Slight violet tint — default in light mode.
settings.themeVariantLightWarmDesc: Warm cream white without a cool cast.
settings.themeVariantLightNordDesc: Polar blue-gray, classic Nord in light mode.
settings.themeColorsLayoutPreview: Module layout (L0 background, L1 navigation, L2 list/content, L3 accent)
settings.themeColorsDarkVariantsHint: Four base looks (same as in the top bar). One click applies the palette immediately.
settings.themeVariantDefaultDesc: Fluent graphite with a slight violet tint.
settings.themeVariantMidnightDesc: Very dark navy with cool blue gradients.
settings.themeVariantNordDesc: Polar Night — lighter blue-grey, classic Nord palette.
settings.themeVariantGraphiteDesc: Neutral warm grey without a color cast — app default.
settings.themeColorsTuneHint: Adjust individual layers. Overrides the selected dark variant or applied preset.
settings.themeColorPresetsHint: Each preset applies to one schema only (light or dark, L0–L3). Custom presets still save your current light and dark combination.
settings.themeColorPresetLimit: Maximum of 24 presets — delete one first.
settings.modulesHint: Choose which areas (Home, Mail, Calendar, Bookings, …) appear as tabs at the top. Re-enable hidden modules here — including Bookings after right-clicking its tab.
settings.modulesOrderHint: Drag the grip on the left to reorder tabs — same order as in the top module bar.
settings.modulesCustomViewsHint: Your own workspaces with a zone grid — create the same way as the plus button in the module bar. They appear to the right of the standard modules.
settings.modulesCustomViewsOrderHint: Order of view tabs in the bar (drag within this list).
settings.modulesCustomViewsEmpty: No custom views yet — use “Create new view” above.
settings.modulesCustomViewDeleteConfirm: Delete view “{{name}}”? The layout cannot be restored afterwards.
settings.languageHint: Sets the language for menus, settings, and hints. Email content is unchanged.
settings.dashboardGridHint: Each tile’s position, width, and height are multiples of this value (in pixels). Gaps between tiles can still be arbitrary.
settings.dashboardGridRange: Allowed: {{min}}–{{max}} px. Default: {{def}} px. After you change the value (on blur), tiles realign to the new grid.
settings.weatherIntro: Search for a place and save it — the weather tile shows current conditions and the next seven days (Open-Meteo, no API key).
settings.weatherGeocodeEmpty: No match — try a more specific place name.
settings.loginIntro: Usually the app uses the vendor’s preconfigured OAuth app (build environment). You only connect your accounts in the browser. Open the section below only if you want to use your own Azure or Google Cloud registration.
settings.oauthSub: Advanced — store client IDs and optional Google client secret locally
settings.azureIntro: Application (client) ID — only needed if you do not use a preconfigured ID. Saving empty removes the local override (the build default ID applies again, if set).
settings.azureActive: Microsoft client ID is active (preconfigured or saved).
settings.googleOAuthIntro: OAuth client ID from Google Cloud Console (Desktop). Client secret is optional: leave empty for PKCE with a public desktop client (Google native app OAuth). Enable Gmail and Calendar APIs. Loopback redirect:
settings.googlePlaceholderSecretStored: Client secret (leave blank = unchanged or PKCE without secret)
settings.googleActive: Google client ID is active. Client secret is only required if your Google project demands one.
settings.notionIntro: Send mail and events as blocks to Notion pages. If the developer portal won't save: use internal integration (recommended).
settings.notionInternalIntro: notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → Internal. Copy the secret token. On each target page: ⋯ → Connections → Add connection. No redirect URI needed.
settings.notionInternalShareHint: With internal integration: share target pages with the integration in Notion (Connections).
settings.notionOAuthSummary: Public integration (OAuth) — only if redirect URI can be saved
settings.notionOAuthHint: Notion always prepends https:// to redirect URIs. Do not use mailclient:// or http:// — only the “Enter in portal” line. After saving it should show https://127.0.0.1:…
settings.notionConnectDisabledTitle: Save client ID and secret first
settings.notionFavoritesEmpty: No favorites yet. Search for a page below to add one.

aiConnections.heading: AI connections
aiConnections.hint: Semantic link suggestions via cloud AI (Gemini/OpenAI) or locally via Ollama. Only metadata is sent — no full mail body or attachments (excerpt optional).
aiConnections.providerHint: Suggestions and graph scan use this provider only.
aiConnections.activeKeyMissing: No API key stored for the selected provider yet.
aiConnections.ollamaModelMissing: Select or enter an Ollama model (e.g. nemotron3:33b).
aiConnections.ollamaBaseUrlHint: Default: http://127.0.0.1:11434 — Ollama must be running (`ollama serve`).
aiConnections.ollamaModelsEmpty: No models found. Run e.g. `ollama pull nemotron3:33b` first.
aiConnections.ollamaLocalHint: Data stays on your machine (no cloud API key). Large models can be slow.
aiConnections.ollamaCompactPrompts: Small model detected: Chronell uses shorter prompts and fewer candidates (better JSON reliability).
aiConnections.embeddingsHint: Builds local embeddings via Ollama (e.g. nomic-embed-text). Suggestions are faster; the LLM is only used for top candidates.
aiConnections.keyStored: Key is stored securely on this device.
aiConnections.snippetModeHint: “Ask every time” shows a preview before each AI call. “Always” sends the excerpt without asking (after consent).
aiConnections.snippetConsentBody:
In addition to metadata, Chronell may send a shortened excerpt (mail snippet/preview, note or event text, max. 500 characters). This increases token usage and privacy exposure.

You can turn this off anytime.
aiConnections.domainProfilesHint: Keywords for retrieval and AI focus (scan and suggestions). Comma-separated.
aiConnections.minConfidenceHint: AI suggestions below this threshold are hidden (panel and scan).
aiConnections.compareProvidersHint: Both providers are queried in parallel; only suggestions both return are shown (✓✓). Doubles API calls.
aiConnections.showLinkQualityOnGraphHint: After “Check with AI” in the connections panel: green = strong, amber = weak, red = questionable (selected node as anchor).
aiConnections.backupNote: Settings backup includes AI options and dismissed suggestions. API keys stay in the secure store and may need to be re-entered after import.
aiConnections.consentBody:
Chronell sends only subjects, names, dates, and short fields to the selected AI provider — never full mail or note bodies.

Suggestions are not saved automatically; you confirm each link yourself.
aiConnections.consentBodyOllama:
Chronell sends metadata (and optionally a short excerpt) to Ollama on your machine — not to a cloud service.

Suggestions are not saved automatically; you confirm each link yourself.

cloudSync.heading: Cloud sync
cloudSync.intro: Syncs notes, connections, rules, workflow, UI preferences, and account preferences (including signature templates per mail account) via Supabase — not your mail (that still comes from Microsoft/Google on each device). Choose local-only or sign in for cloud sync.
cloudSync.notConfigured: Supabase is not set in the build environment. Add CHRONELL_SUPABASE_URL and CHRONELL_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to .env and restart the app.
cloudSync.loginIntro: Sign in with Microsoft 365 (recommended) or use a one-time email code.
cloudSync.conflictHint: Cloud and this device have different snapshots. Automatic sync is paused — choose which version to keep.
cloudSync.conflictRemoteOnly: The cloud was updated from another device.
cloudSync.resultSkippedConflict: Conflict — choose cloud or local above
cloudSync.autoSyncOn: Automatic sync is on (about every {{minutes}} minutes and after note, link, or signature changes).
cloudSync.pollIntervalHint: Between 2 and 30 minutes. After local changes, Chronell still syncs after about 5 seconds.

settings.backupAiConnectionsNote: AI connections settings and dismissed suggestions are included in the backup; Gemini/OpenAI API keys are not — they are stored separately in the secure store.
settings.backupIntro: Exports the full app configuration (e.g. OAuth client IDs, sync range), the entire renderer local storage (appearance, layout, calendar/mail sidebar, dashboard, etc.), account preferences (color, signature templates, calendar lookahead, order), Notion destinations, and from the local database: mail rules, QuickSteps, templates/snippets, meta folders, workflow boards, VIP senders, triage folders, calendar color overrides, pending scheduled sends, notes including links (calendar/task/note; mail only when the message exists locally). No email bodies, no OAuth tokens — signed-in accounts stay connected; meta folders that pin local folder IDs may need a tweak after a clean reinstall. The file may contain client secrets and should not be shared.
settings.importConfirmBody: The file overwrites app configuration, renderer local storage, mail rules, VIP list, workflow board, and triage folder mappings (if present in the file). Your accounts and sign-ins are preserved; email is not imported. The app will reload afterwards.

backupContents.noDatabaseExtras: No database section in the file — rules, notes, etc. will stay unchanged.
backupContents.noSecureExtras: No secure section (older format) — signatures and Notion destinations are missing.

warning.format_v1_no_secure_extras: Older format (v1): no signatures, Notion destinations, or AI settings.
warning.no_database_extras: No database section — rules, notes, and workflow will not be changed on import.
warning.no_oauth_tokens: No OAuth tokens and no mail content.
warning.no_api_keys: AI API keys are not included.
warning.may_contain_client_secrets: The file may contain OAuth client IDs or secrets — do not share.

autoBackup.heading: Automatic backup
autoBackup.intro: After major changes (notes, rules, workflow, signatures, dashboard/theme, etc.) a JSON file is saved to the chosen folder after about 2 minutes: mailclient-einstellungen-latest.json plus a dated copy (max. 5).
autoBackup.pickFolderHint: Auto-backup is on — please choose a target folder.

settings.localDataIntro: Under %APPDATA%\MailClient you will find the SQLite database (mail, calendar cache, tasks), account tokens (encrypted), images, and the app Chromium cache. For a lightweight settings-only backup use the JSON export above; for a full snapshot of this PC use the ZIP archive.
settings.localDataReclaimable: About {{size}} of cache/temp data can be freed.
settings.localDataAttachmentStale: Including {{size}} stale attachments (older than 7 days — removed on startup and when opening attachments).
settings.localDataOptimizedRestartHint: Chromium cache on disk (~500 MB) is fully removed only after restarting the app — please quit MailClient and open it again.
settings.localDataImportConfirmBody: The ZIP overwrites the entire local app data folder (database, cache, images, config files). The app will restart afterward. Only use archives from the same app or after a fresh install.
settings.dialogResizeTitle: Drag to adjust width and height
settings.msNoClientTitle: No Microsoft client ID (build or settings)
settings.googleConfigureFirstTitle: Configure Google client ID first (General or build default)
settings.accountsIntro: Connect or remove accounts. “Sign in again” opens authentication for the same account (e.g. new API permissions). OAuth details only under General → Custom OAuth app, if needed.

accountPermissions.title: Why does Chronell request so many permissions?
accountPermissions.summaryClosed: Explanation of Microsoft and Google permissions when connecting
accountPermissions.intro: When you connect an account, Microsoft or Google shows a long list — that can feel alarming. Chronell is a full mail and productivity client: each permission maps to a feature you can use in the app (inbox, calendar, tasks, contacts, Teams, cloud attachments). Your data is not sold to third parties.
accountPermissions.privacyNote: Sign-in tokens and synced content stay on your computer. Chronell uses permissions only to work with your Microsoft or Google account — not for ads or profiling.
accountPermissions.unverifiedNote: The “unverified” label is normal for desktop apps not published in the Microsoft Store. You still see exactly what you approve, and you can disconnect any account under Accounts at any time.

offline.label: Maintain access to data you have given it access to
offline.purpose: Lets Chronell sync in the background without signing you in again on every launch.

userRead.label: Sign you in and read your profile
userRead.purpose: Your name, email address, and profile photo in the account list and UI.

mailReadWrite.label: Read and write access to your mail
mailReadWrite.purpose: Sync inbox and folders, read mail, move, delete, mark read, and run rules/QuickSteps.

mailSend.label: Send mail on your behalf
mailSend.purpose: Send new messages and replies — only when you press Send.

mailboxSettings.label: Read and write your mailbox settings
mailboxSettings.purpose: Outlook categories (master categories), signature templates, and similar mailbox options in Chronell.

calendars.label: Full access to your calendars
calendars.purpose: View, create, edit, and delete events — including reminders and calendars in the app.

calendarsShared.label: Read calendars you can access
calendarsShared.purpose: Shared and delegated calendars you are allowed to see in Outlook.

groups.label: Group memberships & group calendars
groups.purpose: Microsoft 365 groups and their team calendars in the calendar view.

tasks.label: Create, read, update, and delete your tasks and projects
tasks.purpose: Sync and edit Microsoft To Do / Planner task lists in Chronell.

contacts.label: Full access to your contacts
contacts.purpose: Show and manage Outlook contacts in the People module.

people.label: Read a list of your relevant contacts
people.purpose: Recipient suggestions when composing mail (frequently used addresses).

directory.label: Read basic profiles of all users
directory.purpose: Suggest colleagues in your organization in the To field (directory lookup).

chat.label: Read/write chat messages & create chats
chat.purpose: Show Microsoft Teams chats in Chronell and send messages (when you use that feature).

meetings.label: Read and create your online meetings
meetings.purpose: Add or edit Teams meeting links on calendar events.

onedrive.label: Full access to all files you can access
onedrive.purpose: Attach OneDrive files or use sharing links when composing mail.

sharepoint.label: Edit or delete items in all site collections
sharepoint.purpose: SharePoint and Teams files for cloud attachments and sharing in the composer.

bookings.label: Bookings information & appointments
bookings.purpose: Business Bookings pages and appointments for Chronell’s Bookings integration.

ews.label: Exchange Web Services (separate prompt possible)
ews.purpose: Optional second step for some mailboxes: faster sync via Exchange instead of Graph only — if you enable it in settings.

profile.label: Profile and sign-in (openid, email)
profile.purpose: Identify your account and show your name and profile photo in the app.

gmail.label: Read, send, and manage Gmail
gmail.purpose: Sync inbox, send mail, move, delete, and manage folders — standard for a mail client.

calendar.label: Google Calendar
calendar.purpose: View and edit events in Chronell.

tasks.label: Google Tasks
tasks.purpose: Sync task lists and manage tasks in the app.

contacts.label: Google Contacts (People API)
contacts.purpose: Contacts in the People module and recipient suggestions when composing mail.

settings.msReconnectTitle: Sign in to Microsoft again (token and permissions)
settings.googleReconnectTitle: Sign in to Google again (refresh token)
settings.clearMailCacheConfirm:
All locally cached mail, folders, and sync state for {{email}} will be deleted. That includes in-app mail To Dos, related notes, and mail↔cloud-task links; for Microsoft accounts, also the cached Outlook master categories. Nothing is changed on the server mailbox.

When online, the app re-syncs immediately afterward. When offline, sync resumes on the next connection (or automatically when the app goes online).
settings.clearMailCacheDoneOnline: Mail cache was cleared and the account was re-synced.
settings.clearMailCacheDoneOffline: Mail cache was cleared. The app will sync again once you are online.
settings.clearTasksCacheConfirm:
All locally cached To Do lists and tasks for {{email}} will be deleted, including sync timestamps and in-app planned times for cloud tasks (calendar/work). Mail↔cloud-task links in the database are kept. Nothing changes on the server (Microsoft To Do / Google Tasks).

When online, the app re-fetches tasks from the cloud in the background (this can take several minutes with very large accounts). When offline, sync resumes on the next connection (or automatically when the app goes online).
settings.clearTasksCacheDoneOnline: Tasks cache was cleared. Lists and tasks are being re-fetched from the cloud in the background (this can take a few minutes for large mailboxes).
settings.clearTasksCacheDoneOffline: Tasks cache was cleared. The app will load tasks again once you are online.
settings.accountOnlineTitle: Open the provider account page in your default browser (password, security, subscription)
settings.accountColorHint: Stripe in the sidebar and lists — pick a preset or a custom colour.
settings.accountAvatarHint: Provider photo, initials, icon, or your own image.
settings.accountAvatarProviderNote: Provider photo only when «Profile photo» is selected.
settings.syncWindowIntro: Limits how far back new mail is synced. Saves storage and bandwidth for large mailboxes. Already downloaded older mail is kept.
settings.mailPollIntervalIntro: How often inbox, sent items, and drafts are checked in the background via delta sync. Shorter intervals deliver new mail faster but use more Microsoft and Google API quota.
settings.mailPollIntervalHint: Manual sync (sidebar or refresh) still runs immediately regardless of this setting.
settings.microsoftMailTransportIntro: Controls how Chronell fetches mail for Microsoft accounts (Outlook, Microsoft 365). Calendar, tasks, and contacts always use Microsoft Graph — regardless of this setting.

microsoftMailTransportHint.graph: Reliable for Outlook Online and Microsoft 365. Same API path as calendar and tasks in Chronell.
microsoftMailTransportHint.ews: Classic Exchange protocol. Mainly for on-premises Exchange. If the inbox stays empty or sync fails, choose Graph.
microsoftMailTransportHint.auto: Uses EWS when an EWS token is available. In rare cases this can leave the inbox empty — Graph is usually safer.

settings.microsoftMailTransportChangeNote: After a change, Microsoft accounts are synced once.
settings.mailBodyIndexIntro: Loads mail bodies in the background so global search can find messages you have not opened yet. Higher speed uses more Microsoft/Google API quota.
settings.mailBodyIndexEnabledTitle: Index mail bodies in the background
settings.mailBodyIndexEnabledHint: When off, bodies load only when you open a message. Search still uses subject, sender, and preview text.

mailPreviewMeta.heading: Metadata in mail preview
mailPreviewMeta.intro: Fields below the subject in the reading pane: show or hide and reorder with drag & drop.
mailPreviewMeta.orderHint: Top = further left in the metadata row. In the preview: tap «Arrange», drag fields, then «Done» to save.

mailCompose.heading: Compose email
mailCompose.intro: Default formatting and behavior for new messages, replies, and forwards.
mailCompose.defaultFontSizeHint: Applies to newly typed text and new drafts (in points, pt).
mailCompose.defaultFontFamilyHint: Stored inline in the message — recipients only see the font if it is installed.
mailCompose.defaultTextColorHint: Color for newly composed mail text.
mailCompose.defaultEditorThemeHint: Light/dark for the writing area only — independent of the app theme.
mailCompose.editorScaleHint: Scales only the compose surface — not the sent font size.
mailCompose.editorScaleShortcuts: In the editor: Ctrl + Plus/Minus to zoom, Ctrl + 0 to reset.
mailCompose.defaultImportanceHint: Preset for new messages (can be changed per mail).
mailCompose.readReceiptDefaultHint: Enables read receipt in message options for new mails.

mailListHover.heading: Hover quick actions
mailListHover.intro: Icons shown on the right when you hover a mail row. Enable, disable, and reorder them with drag and drop.
mailListHover.orderHint: Top = further left in the bar. Disabled actions are hidden.

quickSteps.heading: Quick Steps
quickSteps.intro: Custom action chains for the mail list (like Outlook Quick Steps). Actions run in sequence — logically ANDed.
quickSteps.empty: No Quick Steps yet. Create one or use the defaults from first setup.
quickSteps.editorHint: Add actions that run on the selected message when this Quick Step is executed.
quickSteps.ms365Note: Note: Quick Steps are stored locally in MailClient. Microsoft Graph has no API for Outlook Quick Steps — they do not sync to Outlook on the web or desktop. Back up or restore them via Settings → Backup.
quickSteps.enabledLabel: Enabled (shown in pickers and hover bar)
quickSteps.actionsAndHint: All listed actions run one after another.
quickSteps.noActions: No actions yet — pick one below.

errors.action_incomplete: An action is incomplete (e.g. missing folder or tag).

settings.autoImagesHint: Images load directly from servers. For privacy this can enable tracking pixels. When off, you can load images per message manually.
settings.gravatarHint: Profile photos from gravatar.com based on email address. Off by default: initials, address book contact photos, and your account profile photo only. No external requests to Gravatar.
settings.flaggedMailboxFilterHint: For the “Mailbox flag” list filter, only threads count where at least one message is actively flagged outside “Deleted Items” and “Junk”. This trims legacy flags left in deleted/spam-like folders — separate from Microsoft To Do. To remove flags on the server entirely, use Outlook or Graph/PowerShell.
settings.bulkUnflagSettingsHeading: Remove flags on the server (OWA / Outlook)
settings.bulkUnflagSettingsBody: Clears the follow-up / flag state for all flagged messages that are already synced into this app for the selected account, via Microsoft 365 or Gmail APIs. After sync, Outlook on the web and mobile should match. Messages never downloaded here are not touched.
settings.bulkUnflagIntro: Walks flagged messages in the local mail cache for the selected account and updates each one at the provider. OWA and other clients should reflect the change after a short sync.
settings.bulkUnflagNeedAccount: Connect a Microsoft or Google mail account first.
settings.bulkUnflagExcludeDeletedJunk: Only messages outside Deleted Items and Junk (recommended)
settings.bulkUnflagCountUnknown: Re-open the dialog or change options to refresh the count.
settings.bulkUnflagNothing: No flagged messages match the current options.
settings.bulkUnflagConfirm1: Really clear flags for {{count}} messages on the server? This cannot be undone from the app.
settings.bulkUnflagConfirm2: Second confirmation: this bulk action writes to your mailbox.
settings.bulkUnflagOffline: You must be online to run this action.
settings.mailSidebarFoldersIntro: Per account, choose which folders appear in the left mail navigation. Hidden folders remain available (e.g. move, search); the inbox cannot be hidden. Use “Remove from sidebar…” in the folder context menu for a quicker toggle.
settings.triageIntro: When you add a to-do or terminate a message, the app can move it to “In progress” — regardless of its current folder (if mapped). After “Done” (complete to-do) it moves to “Done”. In Gmail, those folders are labels. Without an “In progress” mapping, the message stays where it is.
settings.triageNeedMailAccount: Connect at least one Microsoft or Gmail account under “Accounts”.
settings.wfErrTwoFolders: Please pick two different folders or leave one side empty.
settings.signaturesIntro: Signature templates per mail account — inserted when composing under “Signature / footer”. In the composer, pick a template, edit it, and use “Update template” to save without creating a new one each time.
settings.signaturesNeedAccount: Connect at least one Microsoft or Gmail account under “Accounts”.
settings.categoriesIntro: Master categories like in Outlook; assign per message in the reader under “Categories”. Managing them requires the “MailboxSettings” permission — reconnect Microsoft after an app update if needed.
settings.categoriesNeedAccount: For Microsoft 365 accounts only. Please connect an account under “Accounts” first.
settings.calendarWorkspaceIntro: Events, Gantt timeline, and layers for mail to-dos, cloud tasks, and notes — with inbox and preview panels.
settings.calendarDefaultViewHint: Day, week, month, list, year, or Gantt when opening the module.
settings.calendarRememberViewHint: Use the last selected view on your next visit instead of the default.
settings.calendarLayersIntro: Which overlay layers are on when you first open the calendar (can be toggled in the view).
settings.calendarTimelineIntro: The bottom timeline shows events and tasks in the selected window.
settings.calendarTimelineAutoDismissHint: Past items disappear from the timeline after a short while.
settings.calendarAdvancedIntro: Time zone, Book with me, API lookahead, and calendar visibility in the sidebar.
settings.calendarTzIntro: Controls how event times are shown and the time used when creating Teams meetings against Microsoft 365. “Automatic” uses the Windows system time zone.
settings.calendarApiIntro: Per account: how far from today events are fetched from Microsoft 365 or Google Calendar. A shorter horizon means less data and often faster loads.
settings.calendarConnectHint: Connect a Microsoft or Google account with calendar under “Accounts”.
settings.calendarSidebarIntro: Choose which calendars are listed on the left in Calendar view (same as “Remove from sidebar…” in the context menu). The default calendar slot always stays visible. Calendars are grouped by connected account.
settings.bookWithMeIntro: Save the link to your personal Microsoft booking page. In Outlook on the web, open Book with me and copy the link next to “Personal booking page”.
settings.bookWithMeHint: Booked appointments appear in your calendar automatically. Configure meeting types and availability in Outlook on the web.
settings.bookWithMeHostHint: This URL does not look like a typical Outlook booking page — check the link from Outlook.
settings.bookWithMeMicrosoftOnly: Book with me requires a connected Microsoft 365 account (under Accounts).
settings.bookingsOverviewIntro: Team booking pages, services, and appointments in the app. Publish and manage pages in Outlook on the web.
settings.bookingsMicrosoftOnly: Business Bookings requires a connected Microsoft 365 account with Bookings licensing and the correct Graph permissions.
settings.bookingsTopbarHint: You can hide the Bookings tab via right-click on the tab. Show it again here or under General → Modules.
settings.bookingsTopbarShow: Show Bookings tab in the top bar
settings.bookingsAllModulesLink: Manage all modules in the bar…
settings.bookingsRangeHint: How many days of appointments and calendar to load in the Bookings module.
settings.bookingsPersonalIntro: Your personal booking link for 1:1 meetings — separate from business Bookings. Set the link under Calendar settings.
settings.bookingsOpenBookWithMe: Open Book with me in Calendar settings
settings.bookingsAccessIntro: Business Bookings needs delegated permissions in your Entra app registration. After adding them: admin consent, then reconnect the Microsoft account under Accounts.
settings.bookingsReconnectHint: After changing OAuth scopes, remove and sign in again with the affected Microsoft account under Accounts.
settings.calendarSidebarGroupCalendarsEmpty: No group calendars found or insufficient permissions.
